blocks.text: World·New

The beloved hippo Fiona died Thursday at the Cincinnati Zoo after eating a knit hat that was accidentally tossed into her enclosure earlier this month. Here's a look back at the life of the famous hippo.
9-year-old's death Thursday sparks outpouring of grief at Cincinnati Zoo and beyond
Tributes are pouring in for Fiona, the beloved hippopotamus of the Cincinnati Zoo, who died Thursday after eating a knit hat that was accidentally tossed into her enclosure earlier this month.
Here's a look back at the life of the famous hippo, who became a social media darling after she survived a premature birth.
Against all odds
The zoo shared Fiona's miraculous survival story in videos and blog posts, capturing hearts around the world. Below, the baby hippo makes her media debut in the Hippo Cove at the zoo in May 2017.
(Liz Dufour/USA TODAY NETWORK/Imagn Images/Reuters)
Fiona weighed 13 kilograms when she was born six weeks prematurely in 2017. (Most hippos are born weighing between 23 and 50 kilograms.)
(John Minchillo/The Associated Press)
The hippo, pictured with mom, did more than help sell T-shirts, bobbleheads and ice cream at the zoo. She became a teaching tool in classrooms and libraries and the subject of a series of books.
Fiona on the day her book, Fiona the Hippo, launched on Aug. 7, 2018.
(Albert Cesare/ Enquirer/USA TODAY NETWORK/Imagn Images/Reuters)
Fiona sleeps in her enclosure beside a copy of Saving Fiona by the zoo's director Thane Maynard.
Visitors pose for photographs with a sleeping Fiona on June 26, 2018.
(John Minchillo/The Aasociated Press)
On her third birthday, Jan. 23, 2020, Fiona ate her specialty birthday cake. The zoo used that birthday as a way to raise money for Australian wildlife affected by recent bushfires.
Fiona enjoying the sunshine with Tucker in the Hippo Cove on April 18, 2025.
(Liz Dufour/USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images/Reuters)
A tragic end
On Thursday, Fiona died more than a week after she ate a visitor's hat that accidentally found its way into her enclosure, sparking an outpouring of grief in Cincinnati and beyond.
Here, a young man prepares to place a flower at a memorial for Fiona, as an adult stands nearby at the zoo on Friday.
(Obed Lamy/The Associated Press)
Flowers, handwritten notes, watermelons and other items are displayed at a memorial for Fiona.
With files from The Associated Press
